shower.thought: # 35 Original Shower Thoughts
You only remember the times you remembered to remember, so your life is mostly forgotten moments you forgot to notice.
The most important conversations you'll never have are the ones you assume aren't necessary.
Everyone thinks they're the protagonist of the story, but statistically you're an extra in someone else's.
You can't prove you're conscious, which means no one can prove they aren't faking everything perfectly.
The things you're most afraid to say are usually the things everyone else is thinking too.
You spend your entire life learning how to be an adult, then everyone expects you to have already known.
Time moves slower when you're waiting and faster when you're happy, so your perception of time is just a measure of how much you're not enjoying the present.
We call it "falling" in love, which might be the most honest metaphor we have.
Your phone knows more about your future than you do.
The scariest part of aging isn't looking old—it's realizing how little time you actually have left and how much of it you wasted.
You're nostalgic for a version of your childhood that probably never existed.
Every conversation you have is a negotiation between how you see yourself and how you think the other person sees you.
If you've never been hated by someone, you've probably never stood for anything.
The reason silence is awkward is that it forces you to exist without performing.
You can't remember what it felt like not to know something, so you can never truly understand a beginner's perspective again.
Most of your problems exist because you're too polite to be honest.
Your biggest insecurity is probably obvious to everyone else, who are too busy worrying about theirs to notice.
The internet gave us infinite knowledge but made us lonelier than ever—maybe ignorance wasn't the problem.
You're having a conversation with yourself in your head about conversations you're having out loud.

motivational.thought: The obstacle you're avoiding is the one that will teach you the most. — Unknown
Every expert was once a beginner who refused to quit. — Unknown
Your future self is watching you right now through memories you haven't made yet. — Unknown
Comfort is the enemy of growth, and growth is the only thing that feels like living. — Unknown
The cost of discipline is always less than the cost of regret. — Unknown
You don't rise to the level of your goals; you fall to the level of your systems. — Unknown
Small progress is still progress, and progress is the antidote to despair. — Unknown
The life you want doesn't require you to become a different person. It requires you to become who you already are. — Unknown
Waiting for the perfect moment is just procrastination wearing a crown. — Unknown
Your pain has a purpose if you extract the lesson before it consumes you. — Unknown
The distance between where you are and where you want to be is just a series of ordinary days. — Unknown
What you think about in the shower, you should be working on in the world. — Unknown
Regret multiplies with time, but momentum builds with action. — Unknown
You can't outthink your circumstances. You can only outwork them. — Unknown
The person you'll become in five years is being decided by what you do today. — Unknown
Discipline isn't punishment. It's self-love in action. — Unknown
Most people overestimate what they can do in a year and underestimate what they can do in a decade. — Unknown
Your excuses are the exact size of your fears. — Unknown
The only version of you that matters is the one you're building right now. — Unknown
Starting is the hardest part, but quitting is the longest. — Unknown

darkjoke.thought:
I went to a grief counselor after my dog died.
He said, "Tell me about him." I said, "Well, he's in a better place now." He said, "How do you know?" I said, "He's literally in the ground behind a Whole Foods."

My girlfriend asked why I never want to meet her parents.
I said, "Because the last time I met someone's parents, they asked me what my intentions were. Turns out 'short-term' was the wrong answer."

I told my friend he was being paranoid about his wife cheating.
He said, "How would you know?" I said, "Because I've been sleeping with her for three months and she hasn't noticed."

My therapist asked if I had any regrets.
I said, "Just one." She leaned forward and said, "What is it?" I said, "That you charge by the hour instead of by the breakthrough."

I'm terrible at poker because I can't keep a straight face.
Which is also why my wife found out about my affairs and my mother found out I faked my own death for attention.

The worst part about being colorblind isn't the colors.
It's when you tell someone you're colorblind and they spend twenty minutes explaining what blue looks like while you're just trying to order coffee.

My dad said, "Son, I'm worried you're not taking life seriously enough."
I said, "Dad, you've been dead for six years." He said, "Exactly my point."

I asked my Uber driver if he believed in ghosts.
He said, "Of course not." I said, "Good, because the last passenger never paid me either."

My friend said his therapist suggested he stop catastrophizing.
I said, "That's great advice." He said, "Yeah, it would be if I wasn't already picturing all the ways it could make things worse."

I love my wife, but I hate her mother.
The only thing worse than visiting her is the sinking feeling when you realize your wife is going to turn into her. Then the sinking feeling when you realize you married your mother. Then the sinking feeling when you realize you need to see a therapist.

My doctor told me I have six months to live.
When I couldn't pay the bill, he said, "Don't worry, make it a year."

I got into an argument with my GPS about where to go.
Turns out we both agreed on "straight into a lake," just not for the same reasons.

My wife said I need to be more spontaneous.
So I told her I was leaving her without any warning. She said, "That's not what I meant." I said, "Too late, I already planned it yesterday."

I went to a wedding where the bride got cold feet.
Turned out it was just regular feet—she was just standing in the freezer section of the grocery store where they met.

My friend asked why I never go to the gym anymore.
I said, "Because I realized that 'dying alone' could happen anywhere, so why spend an hour pretending to jog?"

I told my son that life was like a box of chocolates.
He said, "You mean you never know what you're going to get?" I said, "No, I mean eventually everything inside dies."

I'm starting to think my wife's affair isn't actually the problem.
The problem is that I'm relieved to have time alone. The real problem is realizing I married someone specifically to avoid being alone. The actual real problem is that I still prefer the alone part.

My therapist asked what I wanted to get out of therapy.
I said, "A better understanding of myself." She said, "That'll be $200." I said, "Never mind, I hate myself exactly the way I am."

I asked my mom why she never came to my soccer games as a kid.
She said, "Because you were terrible." I said, "So you did come?" She said, "No, your father told me."

I tried online dating and my profile said "No drama."
Turns out that's a red flag that says "I am a lot of drama but I'm in denial about it." My last three matches all ghosted me after the first date. I'm pretty sure one of them is still in my apartment.
